title: URL Filtering actions and their prerequisites

checks.do: Whether override users never receive the prompt, which is checked first on the rule's action and blockOverride fields.
Whether a rule's Allow Override traffic is unrestricted, which depends on SSL inspection and end-user notifications being off.

caution.statement: Caution shows an end-user notification (default or a redirect page) before letting the user through.

quotes: Caution: Select to display an EUN that cautions users before allowing them access to the site.

isolate-needs-zbi.statement: Isolate sends matching traffic through a remote browser using a chosen isolation profile, and exists only when Zero Trust Browser is enabled for the organization.

quotes: Isolate: Select to isolate all the traffic that matches the URL filtering rule through a remote browser.
This action is available only if Zero Trust Browser is enabled for your organization.

conditional-prereqs.statement: Conditional enforces step-up authentication before access. It needs ZIdentity for end users and Client Connector forwarding; through Private or Virtual Service Edges the category is blocked instead, and it does not apply to isolation traffic.

quotes: Conditional Access: Allows access to the selected URL categories by enforcing step-up authentication.
This option is available only if your organization is provisioned with ZIdentity for end users and the traffic forwarding method is Zscaler Client Connector.
conditional access is not supported and the user access to the URL category is blocked with a notification from the browser.
Conditional access doesn't apply to isolation traffic.

override-conditions.statement: Override users and groups take effect only when `blockOverride` is true and the action is BLOCK; override users additionally require that no override groups are set. A rule whose action changed away from BLOCK keeps its stale override list silently.

quotes: Only applies if ``block_override`` is True, ``action`` is `BLOCK` and ``override_groups`` is not set.
Only applies if ``block_override`` is True and ``action`` is `BLOCK`.

override-unrestricted-without-inspection.statement: Traffic matching an Allow Override is permitted without restriction when SSL inspection is off and Show End User Notifications is off in the corresponding SSL inspection rule.

quotes: By default, traffic matching the Allow Override rule is permitted without any restrictions if SSL/TLS Inspection is disabled and the Show End User Notifications option is disabled in the SSL/TLS Inspection rule for the corresponding traffic.

api-action-values.statement: Through the API, `action` also accepts `ICAP_RESPONSE` (hand-off to an ICAP server) and the sentinels `ANY` and `NONE`, which can appear in tenant data although the console rarely sets them.

header-insertion-custom-only.statement: HTTP header insertion on an Allow rule works only for custom URL categories.

quotes: The HTTP custom header insertion works only for custom URL categories.

quotas.statement: Allow and Isolate rules can carry a daily bandwidth quota (10 to 100,000 MB) and a daily time quota (15 to 600 minutes), after which the sites are blocked.

quotes: The minimum value you can enter is 10 MB and the maximum value is 100,000 MB.
The minimum value you can enter is 15 minutes and the maximum value is 600 minutes.

isolate-cbi-profile-get-by-id.summary: Whether GET-by-ID returns cbiProfile for ISOLATE rules

quotes: // API bug workaround: GET by ID does not return the cbiProfile object for ISOLATE rules,

positions.says: The Go SDK says GET by ID does not return cbiProfile for ISOLATE rules while GetAll does, and falls back to GetAll to fill it in.
The Python get_rule issues one GET and parses the rule; it has no fallback.

isolate-cbi-profile-get-by-id.impact: A Python read of an ISOLATE rule by ID can come back without its isolation profile object; read it from the list or use the Go fallback pattern. The Go comment is the only statement of the bug; no capture shows it.
